notes: Read SKILL.md, references/browser-auth.md and references/credential-types.md in full. TypeScript guide to @azure/identity: DefaultAzureCredential, managed identity, service principal (secret/certificate), workload identity, interactive browser and device-code login, developer-tool credentials, chained credentials, sovereign clouds, bearer-token providers, custom TokenCredential, logging, and SPA/browser auth patterns (popup/redirect, React example, CORS, logout).

Medium only because SKILL.md:18,21 and browser-auth.md:12 have `npm install @azure/identity` / `@azure/identity-vscode` (official Microsoft packages, unpinned). All credential use is sample code for the user's application with placeholders or process.env lookups; the skill says never to hardcode credentials or expose client secrets in browser code and does not tell the agent to read, print, or transmit real secrets.

Samples to apply carefully: credential-types.md:353 logs a bearer token to the console, credential-types.md:13 recommends DefaultAzureCredential for production while SKILL.md:322 recommends managed/workload identity for production, and the commented CORS CLI example (browser-auth.md:363-365) uses allowed/exposed headers "*". `fetchTokenFromCustomSource` (credential-types.md:300) is an illustrative user-supplied helper.
